attributes.body:
One of the slightly more formal ways to say that something is happening 'each', or 'every' (A) in Japanese, is by using the prefix 各（かく）. While there is no strict rule for when this prefix can be used, it is almost always seen before words of Chinese origin (kanji compounds), or katakana words.

Although this kanji is used to mark 'each', it is very rarely used to mark units of time. The most common/natural usage of 各（かく） is for identifying things that are part of a sequence. For example:

Each/Every stop, on a train line that has many stops.

Each/Every page, in a book that has many pages.

Each/Every floor, in a building that has many floors.

Each/Every house, in a street of many houses.

Fun Fact

This kanji is used in another word, 各々（おのおの）, which also means 'each', but is primarily used for identifying people.

attributes.description: What is the difference between 各 and 毎ごと?
The Complete Guide To Use それぞれ, 各 and 各々 Easily

attributes.body: Both 各 and それぞれ express the idea of 'each' or 'every', but they differ in usage. 各 always goes before a noun, for example, 各部屋 'each room', 各階 'each floor', and so on. それぞれ, on the other hand, can stand alone at the start of a sentence or be attached to a noun with の. For example, 人はそれぞれ違う意見がある ('People each have differing opinions.').

Both mean 'each', but with different usage. ～ずつ follows quantity expressions to mean 'each' or 'at a time', e.g. 一つずつください 'Give me one of each.' or ちょっとずつよくなってきた 'It's gotten better a little at a time.' 各 appears before nouns and means 'every' or 'each', e.g. この電車は各駅にとまります 'This train stops at every station.'
